finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the q parameter is interpolated directly into the SQL string via an f-string. An attacker can break out of the LIKE literal and run UNION-based queries to read any table in shop.db, such as users or credentials tables if present.
finding.source: request.args.get('q') at app.py:11 (unauthenticated HTTP query parameter)
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12

trace.note: term = request.args.get('q', '') takes attacker input with no validation
term is formatted into the SQL text by an f-string, not bound as a parameter
Query results are returned as JSON, so injected UNION SELECT data is exfiltrated directly

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, escaping, parameterization, authentication or WAF on the route. The other queries in this file (lines 18 and 25) use ? placeholders, so this one is the exception. Flask does not sanitize query strings. sqlite3 execute() allows only one statement per call, so stacked queries are blocked, but UNION-based extraction still works.

verdict.reason: app.py:11 takes q from request.args unvalidated, app.py:12 interpolates it into the SQL via an f-string with no auth, escaping or parameterization (unlike app.py:18 and :25), and app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON, so UNION extraction works for an anonymous attacker.
